newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BEAT BANGLADESH IN RECORD STYLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BEAT BANGLADESH IN RECORD STYLE.

text.p: Saeed Anwar lashed a rapid 90 as Pakistan bounced back from their opening Asia Cup defeat by Sri Lanka to thrash Bangladesh by 109 runs in record-breaking style on Wednesday.
Pakistan piled up the highest-ever total in the one-day tournament, 319 for five in their 50 overs, and dismissed Bangladesh for 210.

Half-centuries from man-of-the-match Anwar, whose 90 off 94 balls included 11 fours, captain Ramiz Raja (52), Inzamam-ul-Haq (77) and Salim Malik (62) helped Pakistan to beat the previous best Cup total, their 284 for three off 45 overs, also against Bangladesh, at Chittagong in 1988.
Bangladesh, despite making their first total in excess of 200 in a one-day international, were all out in the final over, with all-rounder Minhajul Abedin unable to bat due to cramp.
Pakistan recovered from losing opener Aamir Sohail without scoring in the first when Anwar and Ramiz shared a second wicket stand of 123 off 121 balls, a Cup record.
The partnership beat the previous highest of 92 unbroken between Manoj Prabhakar and Navjot Sidhu for India against Bangladesh at Sharjah in 1995.
Anwar was hit on the left eye while attempting to sweep off-spinner Naimur Rahman on 73 and was troubled by the injury sufficiently to bat with dark glasses after treatment.
Inzamam and Malik provided acceleration with a 109-run partnership for the fourth wicket in only 95 balls.

Facing an asking rate of 6.4 runs per over, Bangladesh were soon put on the defensive by Pakistan's Kabir Khan, who removed Naimur Rahman and Habibul Bashar off successive deliveries to reduce them to 13 for two.
However, skipper Akram Khan (59) and opener Athar Khan (82) added 110 for the fourth wicket to give the total some respectability.
They both fell to off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq, who finished with five for 38.
